security.note: No own ACL/rules; relies on payment's security and on base.group_system field groups guarding xendit_public_key / xendit_secret_key / xendit_webhook_token.

views.note: xml_loc=154: payment.provider form inheritance (Xendit public/secret keys + webhook token), QWeb redirect-form template (payment_xendit_templates.xml drives the auto-submit redirect to the Xendit invoice_url), plus payment_provider_data.xml. No own model views.

behavioral_notes.observation: For every non-card payment method, _get_specific_rendering_values builds an invoice payload via _xendit_prepare_invoice_request_payload (external_id=tx.reference, rounded amount, description, customer block with given_names/email/mobile/addresses, success_redirect_url carrying tx_ref + a payment_utils.generate_access_token(reference, amount) + success=true, failure_redirect_url, currency, and a payment_methods[] mapped through const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING -- FPX selections expand to the full const.FPX_METHODS bank list) and POSTs it to 'v2/invoices' via the parent engine's _send_api_request. The Xendit-hosted invoice_url returned is handed to the QWeb redirect template as api_url, so the browser is auto-submitted to Xendit's hosted checkout page. On ValidationError the tx is _set_error and an empty dict is returned. None of this server-to-server HTTP nor the hosted-redirect handoff is visible in Python field/model metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._xendit_create_charge -> POST https://api.xendit.co/credit_card_charges (direct Card / token flow) with secret-key HTTP basic auth
behavioral_notes.observation: The Card path is a direct (non-redirect) flow: the browser tokenizes card details with the Xendit.js SDK, then the jsonrpc route /payment/xendit/payment hands the resulting token_ref to _xendit_create_charge, which POSTs {token_id, external_id=reference, amount, currency, optional authentication_id, is_recurring=True when token_id/tokenize set} to 'credit_card_charges'. Outbound auth is configured in models/payment_provider.py: _build_request_url targets https://api.xendit.co/{endpoint}, _build_request_auth returns (xendit_secret_key, '') -- i.e. HTTP Basic auth with the secret key as username and empty password -- and _parse_response_error pulls response.json()['message']. The actual HTTP is delegated to payment.provider._send_api_request in the parent engine; the response is folded into the state machine via _process('xendit', data). The basic-auth scheme, the api.xendit.co endpoints, and the is_recurring 3DS-skip semantics are invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: XenditController.xendit_webhook (/payment/xendit/webhook) -> x-callback-token verify + _process; xendit_return (/payment/xendit/return) -> _set_pending; reference lookup via _search_by_reference
behavioral_notes.observation: The public, csrf=False POST webhook reads the JSON body, locates the tx with payment.transaction._search_by_reference('xendit', data) (which routes through _extract_reference -> data['external_id']), then calls _verify_notification_token BEFORE _process: it reads the 'x-callback-token' header and rejects (werkzeug Forbidden) if missing or if it fails a constant-time consteq() against provider.xendit_webhook_token. The redirect-return GET route /payment/xendit/return instead only flips a still-draft tx to _set_pending() after re-validating the access_token (check_access_token(access_token, tx_ref, amount)) and success=true, then redirects to /payment/status -- it does NOT trust the redirect for the final state, leaving the authoritative done/cancel/error transition to the signed webhook. _apply_updates writes provider_reference=data['id'], remaps FPX bank codes back to 'fpx', and maps Xendit status (const.PAYMENT_STATUS_MAPPING: PENDING / SUCCEEDED|PAID|CAPTURED / CANCELLED|EXPIRED / FAILED) to _set_pending/_set_done/_set_canceled/_set_error. The token verification, the constant-time compare, and the inbound state transitions are all invisible to metadata.

support_tokenization is force-enabled for code=='xendit' in _compute_feature_support_fields; Card is the sole tokenizable method. When tx.tokenize is set, payment's engine calls _extract_token_values after a successful charge: it vaults provider_ref = payment_data['credit_card_token_id'] and payment_details = last 4 of payment_data['masked_card_number'] (Xendit pads with X's). Subsequent off-session charges re-use that token via _send_payment_request -> _xendit_create_charge(token.provider_ref) with is_recurring=True so they skip 3DS. _get_redirect_form_view returns None for Xendit validation operations to avoid rendering a useless redirect template (Card is always direct).

behavioral_notes.element: external integration surface (gap #7) -- endpoints, keys, SDK
behavioral_notes.observation: Static gap-#7 facts (extract_frontend.py): uses_api_keys=true; one outbound endpoint template -- https://api.xendit.co/{endpoint} -- declared in models/payment_provider.py (_build_request_url). Concrete endpoints reached: v2/invoices (Invoices API v2) and credit_card_charges (Credit Charge API v1) per README. Auth is HTTP Basic with the secret key as username (_build_request_auth). No 'requests' import here: HTTP is delegated to payment.provider._send_api_request in the parent engine, which payment_xendit configures via _build_request_url / _build_request_auth / _parse_response_error overrides. On the browser side the Xendit.js tokenization SDK is loaded (lazily, on payment-form submit) to tokenize card details client-side (SAQ A-EP per README) -- a second, client-side channel to Xendit. This dual server-to-server + client-side acquirer link is the canonical metadata gap #7: none of it is reachable from model/field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (static) -- Xendit.js tokenization + AuthUI 3DS component + PaymentForm patch
behavioral_notes.observation: 3 JS files, 1 OWL component (gap #3). Unlike most acquirers, this module registers an AuthUI OWL component (registry main_components:AuthUI + services:auth_ui) used to render the Xendit 3DS authentication UI, and patches PaymentForm.prototype (static/src/) to drive the Xendit.js SDK: on Card it reads card inputs in clear, hands them straight to Xendit.js to mint a single/multiple-use token, then calls the /payment/xendit/payment jsonrpc route. Assets load into web.assets_frontend (manifest glob static/src/**/*). These browser interactions and the Xendit.js SDK are invisible to Python metadata (gap #3).

external_integrations.sdk: Xendit.js (browser card tokenization); server side uses no python SDK -- HTTP via payment.provider._send_api_request
endpoints: https://api.xendit.co/{endpoint} (v2/invoices Invoices API v2; credit_card_charges Credit Charge API v1)
external_integrations.auth: HTTP Basic auth -- xendit_secret_key as username, empty password (_build_request_auth)
external_integrations.pattern: Concrete realization of metadata gap #7: a real external acquirer integration. Outbound server-to-server REST to api.xendit.co (v2/invoices for the hosted-redirect flow, credit_card_charges for the direct/token Card flow) authenticated with a secret API key via HTTP Basic; a parallel client-side Xendit.js tokenization channel (SAQ A-EP); and inbound settlement via an x-callback-token-verified webhook plus a redirect-return route. The base 'payment' engine flags uses_api_keys but ships no live acquirer -- this module is exactly that override.
external_integrations.note: Prime gap-#7 example: none of the Xendit endpoints, the secret-key Basic auth, the webhook x-callback-token trust, or the browser Xendit.js channel are derivable from Python model/field metadata; they were established only by reading payment_provider.py + payment_transaction.py + controllers/main.py + const.py.

capabilities: Accept Card payments via Xendit (direct credit_card_charges flow with client-side Xendit.js tokenization)
Accept Southeast-Asian e-wallet / bank / QR payments via Xendit hosted Invoice redirect (DANA, OVO, QRIS, FPX, Touch'n Go, PromptPay, LinePay, ShopeePay, ZaloPay, etc.)
3DS authentication via the AuthUI OWL component
Tokenization / Saved Cards (vault Xendit credit_card_token_id; off-session recurring via is_recurring)
Multi-currency acceptance across IDR / MYR / PHP / THB / VND
value_streams: Collect-Payment (Card direct): tokenize card with Xendit.js -> /payment/xendit/payment jsonrpc -> _xendit_create_charge POST credit_card_charges (api.xendit.co) -> _process -> state machine; signed webhook confirms final state

Collect-Payment (redirect/invoice): _get_specific_rendering_values -> POST v2/invoices -> browser redirect to Xendit hosted invoice_url -> /payment/xendit/return (_set_pending) -> async /payment/xendit/webhook (x-callback-token) -> _process -> done/error
Tokenize-and-Recharge: successful Card charge + tokenize -> vault payment.token (credit_card_token_id) -> later off-session _xendit_create_charge(token, is_recurring=True) skipping 3DS
Settle: webhook PAID/SUCCEEDED/CAPTURED -> _set_done -> downstream post-process settlement (account_payment / sale)
information_concepts: payment.transaction (mapped to a Xendit Invoice or credit_card_charge; keyed by external_id=reference)
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; xendit_public_key / xendit_secret_key / xendit_webhook_token are restricted to base.group_system; everything else inherits payment's groups/record rules)
policies: Webhook authenticity: events must pass _verify_notification_token (x-callback-token constant-time consteq against xendit_webhook_token) or are rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden
Redirect-return only flips a still-draft tx to pending and only after check_access_token(access_token, reference, amount) + success=true; final state is left to the signed webhook
Card validation operations render no redirect form (_get_redirect_form_view returns None) since Card is always the direct flow
Supported currencies bounded to const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES (IDR/MYR/PHP/THB/VND), all zero-decimal (const.CURRENCY_DECIMALS), amounts rounded DOWN
Tokenized / recurring charges sent with is_recurring=True so subsequent payments skip 3DS
Public/secret/webhook keys gated by base.group_system field groups
stakeholders: Merchant / Company (res.company, holds the Xendit account & keys)
Xendit (external acquirer / PSP for Indonesia, Philippines and wider SEA)
Accountant (consumes settled payments via account_payment downstream)
metrics: (no own reports; transaction volumes/amounts/state surfaced by the parent payment.transaction pivot/graph)

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_xendit is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: a concrete acquirer adapter whose purpose is to interconnect two parties who would not otherwise transact directly -- the payer (cardholder / e-wallet user) and the merchant -- by linking the merchant to Xendit's Southeast-Asian card / e-wallet / bank / QR network. It exhibits the mediating-technology activities: network promotion & contract management (API-key + webhook-token management, currency/payment-method enablement), service provisioning (creating the Xendit Invoice or credit_card_charge and confirming it per transaction), and infrastructure operation (the server-to-server api.xendit.co link, the Xendit.js client tokenization channel, and the x-callback-token-verified webhook settlement loop). It does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve a bespoke customer problem (shop). It inherits the parent 'payment' engine's value_model exactly: the engine is the generic mediator and this module is its Xendit realization. activity_class is 'support' because, from the enterprise value-chain perspective, payment acceptance is an infrastructure/finance support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False, no end-user app) sitting under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash, with the side of 'manage an external payment provider'. So value_model=network (its own internal logic is mediation, an acquirer integration -- gap #7), activity_class=support (its place on the enterprise value chain). This mirrors the sibling payment_stripe.metamodel.json (network/support) and the parent payment engine.

standard_capabilities: direct Card payment via Xendit credit_card_charges with client-side Xendit.js tokenization (3DS via AuthUI)
hosted-redirect acceptance of SEA e-wallet / bank / QR methods via the Xendit Invoices API (v2/invoices)
tokenization / saved cards (Xendit credit_card_token_id), including off-session recurring (is_recurring)
asynchronous settlement via an x-callback-token-verified webhook plus a redirect-return confirmation route
multi-currency acceptance across IDR / MYR / PHP / THB / VND (zero-decimal rounding)
typical_fits: online shop / portal checkout collecting payments in Indonesia, the Philippines and wider SEA via Xendit
card save-for-later and tokenized recurring/subscription charges (is_recurring credit_card_charges)
e-wallet / QR / bank-transfer collection (DANA, OVO, QRIS, FPX, PromptPay, ShopeePay, ZaloPay, etc.) via hosted invoice redirect
send-a-payment-link or pay-an-invoice-online collection (with account_payment / sale downstream)
common_gaps: no manual capture / authorize-then-capture and no void operation implemented (charge is immediate)
no in-module refund operation (no _send_refund_request override here)
no merchant self-onboarding (Stripe-Connect-style) -- API keys are entered manually on the provider form
the public-URL requirement for webhooks means local/dev instances need a tunnel; without an xendit_webhook_token set the callback verification would have no secret to compare against
currency support bounded to const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES; other currencies are filtered out
bespoke reconciliation / settlement document chains live downstream (account_payment, sale), not here
drive_hints: odoo shell: print([m for m in dir(env['payment.transaction']) if '_xendit' in m])
curl -X POST https://<host>/payment/xendit/webhook (csrf=False, auth=public) with a missing/invalid x-callback-token header -> expect HTTP 403 Forbidden from _verify_notification_token

open_questions: Exact Xendit Invoices API v2 and Credit Charge API v1 request/response payloads beyond the fields built in _xendit_prepare_invoice_request_payload / _xendit_create_charge.
Real-world distribution of Xendit transaction states, method mix (card vs e-wallet vs FPX), and tokenization usage (no runtime row counts captured).
How refunds/chargebacks are handled operationally given no in-module refund override (likely manual via the Xendit dashboard or a downstream module).
Whether instances reliably register the webhook (xendit_webhook_token set) vs rely on the redirect-return route, which only flips draft->pending and never finalizes state.
